title: W04b: reconciliation core operation
description: Implement the single reconciliation operation of plan 7: validate inputs, context, local object identity and task intent before planning any mutation; recover any previous intent and reload tasks, claims and history under the ledger lock; refuse duplicate target task IDs, ambiguous source filenames, invalid schemas or duplicate claim IDs affecting the target, multiple active claims, divergent lifecycle state, unsafe record paths and conflicting evidence metadata. Apply the 7.2 state table exactly, including attach-only on open tasks, the owner and claim requirement for closure, refusal for every other state and for wont_do, attach-only on done tasks, and no_change for an already-satisfied request regardless of retry actor. A close request is all-or-nothing with respect to the new intent and never partially attaches evidence. No-change writes no task, claim, timestamp, metadata or event. Resolve immutable Git data outside the lock where possible, verify a captured ledger revision before committing, and never hold the ledger lock across an unbounded subprocess. Append the 7.5 events in fixed order and return the 7.4 data contract. Implementation baseline: merged main 6276d5f / ledger closure e64d4bd, Waystation 0.6.0 on Bun 1.4.1; see docs/reconciliation-2026-09-27.md. Reuse the merged foundation and its tests. Compose resolveCommitObject, getSourceIdentity, parseCommitTrailers/resolveTaskSelection and the captured InvocationContext. Reuse buildIntent, mutationWrite and the locked record loaders; preserve full descriptions and raw non-UTF-8 bytes. Own core results and event semantics; W06a owns human rendering and transport envelopes. W04c supplies the reopened-lifecycle guard before public closure is exposed.
acceptance: Every row of the 7.2 table is covered, including owner mismatch, non-owner closure, wont_do refusal, done with a new association requiring attach-only, and a repeated request from a different retry actor.
A failed closure attaches nothing; a successful closure updates exactly status, updated_at, closed_at and the active claim's status and completed_at.
No-change emits no writes and no events while still following recovery of a prior interrupted mutation.
The core returns the plan 7.4 structured result for attachment, closure with attachment, closure using existing evidence and no_change; it performs no CLI formatting or MCP transport handling.
Full object and source identity, supplied hash, task source, explicit close input and outcome booleans appear in the audit events, and existing consumers tolerate the additive fields.
notes:
Acceptance groups A04, A05 and A06. The existing commit-attachment helper is not idempotent and carries no source identity, so it must not be the write path; a real association is recorded in the same mutation as the commit reference.

POC-first decision (2026-09-27): deferred behind task-poc-value-review. Keep this full-plan task todo. A completed review, including a negative/stop decision, does not authorize promotion; the owner must explicitly select an MVP scope. Before implementation, inspect POC artifacts and acceptance evidence and reuse or retire them rather than duplicating native UI, adapters or assembly. Full requirements remain preserved here.
